summary: Create the full BW text and dimension style set in the current drawing without changing the active styles
body:
Seeds a drawing with the Beveridge Williams standard styles so the engineering annotation commands have everything they need. It is the first thing to run in a drawing that didn't come from a BW template.

The styles are created on demand and the full specification is re-applied every time, so a style that an older build made wrongly is repaired the next time the command runs.
howto: No prompts — run it and the styles are added. It reports [WSYDrafting] BW styles imported (BW_AN family, BWAN_DIM25/35). on the command line when it's finished.
produces: The BW_AN text-style family — BW_AN (arial narrow, annotative), BW_AN_Italics (arial italic), BW_BK_Lotno (arial black) and BW_AU (arial unicode ms) — plus the BWAN_DIM25 and BWAN_DIM35 annotative dimension styles.
notes: Whatever text style, TEXTSIZE and dimension style were active before you ran it are restored afterwards, so importing the styles never changes what you're currently drawing with.

summary: Reset the drawing's annotation scale list to the standard engineering set
body:
Replaces whatever annotation scales a drawing has accumulated with the office engineering list — the plain ratios plus the named layout scales used on engineering plan sets.

It is deliberately a manual command and never runs on its own, because it wipes the list before rebuilding it.
howto: No prompts and no confirmation. It runs immediately and reports how many scales it removed and added — Scale list reset: N removed, N added.
produces: The named presets Layout Plan, Line Marking, Intersection Detail, Parking Plan, Turning 500 / 250 / 200, Sewer Layout, Water, MD Locality and MD Layout, plus the ratio scales 1:10000, 1:5000, 1:2500, 1:2000, 1:1000, 1:500, 1:250, 1:200, 1:100, 1:50, 1:25, 1:20 and 1:10. Scales that already exist by name are left alone.
notes: Every other scale is removed first. The currently active scale is skipped, and any scale still referenced by annotative objects can't be deleted so it survives — but anything else you had added is gone.

summary: Create annotation scales from a dialog, working out the paper-to-drawing ratio for you
body:
Adds annotation scales one at a time or in batches, using the office convention for metre drawings: paper units are fixed at 1 and the drawing units are the denominator divided by 1000.

This is the same tool as the Add New Scale button on the WSY Drafting ribbon — it ships in the shared toolbox assembly, so both ribbons run exactly the same command.
howto: Opens a dialog rather than prompting on the command line. Enter the drawing units and a name (which auto-fills to the ratio), and add as many as you need before closing. It reports N scale(s) created.
produces: Annotation scale entries in the drawing's scale list. Nothing is drawn. A scale whose name already exists is skipped rather than duplicated.
notes: Scales that arrived through an xref are hidden from the existing-names list — BricsCAD suffixes them _XREF and AutoCAD-style names contain an @. The older prompt-based BWCSCALE has been retired; use CSCALE.

summary: Place or restyle engineering annotation text at 2.5 mm on the T25 layer
body: The smallest of the four BW text heights, for general notes and callouts on engineering plans. Like the rest of the family it does double duty: it places new text, and it reformats text you already have to the standard.
howto: Select the text first and it's reformatted in place — single-line text is converted to MText on the way. Run it with nothing selected and it loops, prompting Text insertion point [ESC to exit] and opening the in-place editor at each point until you press Esc. Empty results are discarded.
produces: Annotative MText in the BW_AN style on layer T25 (yellow), colour ByLayer, line spacing 0.8 at-least. The height is the drawing's TEXTSIZE — set to 2.5 by this command — divided by the current annotation scale value. Reformatted text is attached middle-centre; newly placed text is attached top-left.
notes: Set the right annotation scale before you place text — the height is derived from it.

summary: Place or restyle engineering annotation text at 3.5 mm on the T35 layer
body: The 3.5 mm step of the BW text family — the usual choice for sub-headings and labels that need to read above general note text.
howto: Select the text first and it's reformatted in place — single-line text is converted to MText on the way. Run it with nothing selected and it loops, prompting Text insertion point [ESC to exit] and opening the in-place editor at each point until you press Esc.
produces: Annotative MText in the BW_AN style on layer T35 (green), at a working TEXTSIZE of 3.5 divided by the current annotation scale value.

summary: Place or restyle engineering annotation text at 5 mm on the T50 layer
body: The 5 mm step of the BW text family, for headings and anything that has to stand out on a plotted sheet.
howto: Select the text first and it's reformatted in place — single-line text is converted to MText on the way. Run it with nothing selected and it loops, prompting Text insertion point [ESC to exit] until you press Esc.
produces: Annotative MText in the BW_AN style on layer T50 (cyan), at a working TEXTSIZE of 5.0 divided by the current annotation scale value.

summary: Place or restyle engineering annotation text at 7 mm on the T70 layer
body: The largest of the four BW text heights — plan titles and major headings.
howto: Select the text first and it's reformatted in place — single-line text is converted to MText on the way. Run it with nothing selected and it loops, prompting Text insertion point [ESC to exit] until you press Esc.
produces: Annotative MText in the BW_AN style on layer T70 (blue), at a working TEXTSIZE of 7.0 divided by the current annotation scale value.

summary: Draw a multileader with 2.5 mm text and arrow, matched to the T25 text height
body: Places a multileader whose text height, arrow size and dogleg all match the 2.5 mm BW text standard, so a leader note sits alongside BW25 text without looking out of scale.
howto: Run the command and the native MLEADER takes over — pick the arrow point, then the landing, then type the text.
produces: A multileader on layer T25 using the BWAN_ML25 style: straight leader, dogleg enabled at 2.5, 2.5 mm arrow, annotative MText content in BW_AN at 2.5 mm, leader and text colour ByLayer, landing gap 1.5, attached to the middle of the top line and held horizontal. The style is made current (CMLEADERSTYLE).

summary: Draw a multileader with 3.5 mm text and arrow, matched to the T35 text height
body: The 3.5 mm multileader, sized to sit with BW35 text.
howto: Run the command and the native MLEADER takes over — pick the arrow point, then the landing, then type the text.
produces: A multileader on layer T35 using the BWAN_ML35 style — same specification as the rest of the family, with the text height, arrow size and dogleg length all at 3.5.

summary: Draw a multileader with 5 mm text and arrow, matched to the T50 text height
body: The 5 mm multileader, sized to sit with BW50 text.
howto: Run the command and the native MLEADER takes over — pick the arrow point, then the landing, then type the text.
produces: A multileader on layer T50 using the BWAN_ML50 style, with the text height, arrow size and dogleg length all at 5.0.

summary: Draw a multileader with 7 mm text and arrow, matched to the T70 text height
body: The largest BW multileader, sized to sit with BW70 text.
howto: Run the command and the native MLEADER takes over — pick the arrow point, then the landing, then type the text.
produces: A multileader on layer T70 using the BWAN_ML70 style, with the text height, arrow size and dogleg length all at 7.0.

summary: Draw a horizontal or vertical dimension in the BW engineering style
body: A wrapper around the native DIMLINEAR that sets the DIMS layer and the BW dimension style first, so you never have to remember to switch either.
howto: Run the command and the normal linear dimension prompts follow — pick the two extension line origins, then place the dimension line.
produces: A linear dimension on layer DIMS (white) in the BWAN_DIM25 style: 2.5 mm yellow text in BW_AN, 2.5 mm closed filled arrows, two decimal places, text above the dimension line, and annotative.

summary: Draw a dimension aligned to the two points picked, in the BW engineering style
body: The aligned equivalent of BWDIMLIN — the dimension line runs parallel to the two points rather than orthogonally.
howto: Run the command and the native DIMALIGNED prompts follow — pick the two points, then place the dimension line.
produces: An aligned dimension on layer DIMS in the BWAN_DIM25 style.

summary: Draw an angular dimension in the BW engineering style
body: Dimensions the angle between two lines, or the included angle of an arc or circle, with the BW layer and style already set.
howto: Run the command and the native DIMANGULAR prompts follow — pick the two lines (or the arc), then place the dimension arc.
produces: An angular dimension on layer DIMS in the BWAN_DIM25 style. Angular decimal places are set to 0 in that style.

summary: Draw an arc length dimension in the BW engineering style
body: Dimensions the length along an arc rather than the chord — used on kerb returns and curved alignments.
howto: Run the command and the native DIMARC prompts follow — select the arc or polyline arc segment, then place the dimension.
produces: An arc length dimension on layer DIMS in the BWAN_DIM25 style.

summary: Draw a radius dimension on a circle or arc in the BW engineering style
body: Labels the radius of a circle or arc with the BW layer and dimension style already set.
howto: Run the command and the native DIMRADIUS prompts follow — select the circle or arc, then place the dimension text.
produces: A radius dimension on layer DIMS in the BWAN_DIM25 style.

summary: Draw a diameter dimension on a circle or arc in the BW engineering style
body: Labels the diameter of a circle or arc — typically pipes and pits — with the BW layer and dimension style already set.
howto: Run the command and the native DIMDIAMETER prompts follow — select the circle or arc, then place the dimension text.
produces: A diameter dimension on layer DIMS in the BWAN_DIM25 style.

summary: Plot the current layout to an A1 PDF at 1:1 and open it
body: One-click PDF of the sheet you're looking at, at full A1 size. It drives the native -PLOT command with a fixed token stream, so there is nothing to set up and nothing to get wrong.
howto: Open the layout you want and run the command — there are no prompts. When the plot finishes the PDF is opened for you.
produces: A PDF written to your Documents folder, named drawing-layout.pdf after the drawing and the current layout, plotted through Print as PDF.pc3 on A1 media, millimetres, landscape, extents, centred, at 1:1.
notes: Paper space only — in model space it says This function can only be used in paper space. and stops. If the Print as PDF.pc3 device isn't installed it refuses to start rather than half-plotting, and tells you to reinstall the suite. If you cancel the plot, or the PDF doesn't appear where it was expected, it says so on the command line instead of opening anything.

summary: Plot the current layout to an A3 PDF at 1:2 and open it
body: The half-size check print of the same sheet — an A1 layout reduced to A3. Used for markups and issue copies.
howto: Open the layout you want and run the command — there are no prompts. When the plot finishes the PDF is opened for you.
produces: A PDF written to your Documents folder, named drawing-layout.pdf, plotted through Print as PDF.pc3 on A3 media, millimetres, landscape, extents, centred, at 1:2.
notes: Paper space only, and it needs the Print as PDF.pc3 device — same conditions as BWPDFA1.

summary: Print the current layout as an A3 hard copy on the survey room printer
body: Sends the sheet you're on straight to the survey room printer at A3, without going through the plot dialog.
howto: Open the layout you want and run the command — there are no prompts. A message box confirms The layout "…" has been printed to "WSY-SurveyRoom". when it's done.
produces: A hard copy through the WSY-SurveyRoom.pc3 device on A3 (297 × 420 mm) media, millimetres, landscape, extents, centred, at 1:2. Nothing is added to the drawing.
notes: Paper space only. If the device isn't installed the command stops before sending anything, and if the plot is cancelled or fails you get a command-line message rather than the confirmation dialog.

summary: Update title-block attributes across the drawing's layouts from a CSV register
body:
Fills in every title block in the drawing from a shared CSV, so a project's sheet numbers, titles, dates and revisions are maintained in one spreadsheet rather than sheet by sheet.

The drawing folder holds a pointer file, _DWGLISTCSV.TXT, whose first line names the CSV. In the CSV the first column is the drawing name, the second is the layout, and every remaining column heading is an attribute tag.
howto: No prompts — run it and it reports either --> Attributes are up-to-date. or --> N attributes updated in N blocks. Everything else it has to say is a diagnostic: the pointer file being missing or empty, the CSV not being found, the file not being a .csv, or this drawing's name not appearing in the first column.
produces: Changes attribute values on block references in the layouts named in the CSV. Only attributes whose tag matches a column heading and whose value actually differs are touched; nothing is created or erased.
notes: Drawing names and layout names are matched case-insensitively, and the drawing name is compared without its extension. The CSV is read using the machine's regional list separator, falling back to a comma.

summary: Open the job's drawing register spreadsheet from the current drawing's folder
body: A shortcut to the register that sits beside the drawings, so you don't have to go looking for it in Explorer.
howto: No prompts — run it and the register opens. It looks in the current drawing's folder for the first file matching *_Drawing_Register.xls*, so both .xls and .xlsx registers are found.
produces: Nothing in the drawing — it opens the spreadsheet in whatever application is registered for it.
notes: The drawing has to have been saved. If the folder can't be resolved you get Drawing folder not found (unsaved drawing?)., and if there's no register beside it, File not found.

summary: Open the current drawing's folder in Windows Explorer
body: Opens the folder the active drawing lives in — handy for grabbing a reference, checking the rasters folder or dropping a PDF next to the DWG.
howto: No prompts — run it and Explorer opens at the drawing's folder.
produces: Nothing in the drawing.
notes: The drawing has to have been saved; an unsaved drawing has no folder and you'll get Drawing folder not found (unsaved drawing?).

summary: Drag text along a curve or multileader so it follows the geometry
body:
Aligns new or existing text to a polyline, arc, spline or multileader by dragging it along the target — the text rotates to follow the curve as you move, and you click to drop it. It's the tool for labelling pipes, alignments and boundaries where the label has to sit on the line.

The same drag machinery is shared with the drafting ribbon's CLABEL, and the settings dialog is common to both.
howto:
It loops until you exit. At Select text to align [New/Settings] <Exit>: pick existing text or mtext, choose New and answer Specify text <select>: to create some, or choose Settings to open the dialog. Then Select curve or multileader to align to: — curves nested inside blocks and xrefs are valid targets. Drag the text into place and click. Esc or Enter at the first prompt exits.

The dialog controls the object type for new text (text or mtext), justification, offset factor, rotation, readable orientation, background mask and its offset, plus Multiple and Copy modes and the layer and text style used for new text. Settings persist between sessions.
produces: Moves and rotates the text you selected, or creates new text or mtext using the type, justification, layer and style set in the dialog. With Copy selected on, the original is left alone and a copy is placed; with Multiple on, it keeps dragging a fresh copy after each click.
notes: Cancelling a drag restores the original text rather than leaving it half-moved. Text on a locked layer is reported as not editable and skipped.

summary: Generate closed polylines or regions outlining every object in a selection
body:
Traces the outline around a set of objects. It builds a temporary rectangular frame just outside the selection's extents and then uses the native BOUNDARY command to construct outlines around every island inside that frame.

This is Lee Mac's Outline Objects routine, carried in the suite's Community LISP tools component rather than compiled into the plugin.
howto: Select the objects to outline, then answer Erase original objects? [Yes/No] <Yes>: — the default erases them and leaves only the outline.
produces: One or more closed polylines or regions on the current layer, following whatever the native BOUNDARY command produces for the selection.
notes: Requires the Community LISP tools component to be installed; without it the command isn't defined.

summary: Draw a model space polyline showing the extent of a paper space viewport
body:
Constructs a polyline in model space representing what a paper space viewport actually shows, accounting for the viewport's position, scale, rotation and view direction. Useful for checking coverage before issuing a sheet set, or for building a key plan.

This is Lee Mac's Viewport Outline routine, carried in the suite's Community LISP tools component. Two variants come with it: VPOL outlines every viewport in the active layout, and VPOA every viewport in every layout.
howto: Switch to a layout with no viewport active, then run it and answer Select viewport:. In model space it refuses with Command not available in Modelspace.
produces: A 2D (LW) polyline in model space tracing the transformed viewport boundary. Rectangular, polygonal and clipped viewports are all handled, including arc segments.
notes: Requires the Community LISP tools component. The polyline's properties and optional interior offset are fixed in that routine's own parameters section.

summary: Convert closed curves into wipeouts, including ones with arcs
body: Turns circles, ellipses and polylines into wipeouts. The native wipeout command only accepts straight-segment polylines, so this samples curved geometry into enough vertices to keep the shape.
howto: Select the objects first if you like, otherwise it asks for a selection filtered to circles, ellipses and polylines. Then Do you want to keep the original entities? [Yes/No]:, defaulting to Yes.
produces: One wipeout per valid object, on the current layer. Circles and ellipses are sampled at 50 points; polyline arc segments at 1 + 25 × √|bulge| points. It reports Wipeouts created for the selection set (N).
notes: Objects that can't be sampled into at least three points are silently skipped.

summary: Strip inline formatting codes from mtext, multileaders, dimension overrides and attributes
body:
Removes every inline formatting code — colour, font, height, width, oblique, tracking, underline, overline, alignment and paragraph codes, plus stacked fractions and grouping braces — leaving plain content that picks up its appearance from the text style.

It is a no-dialog strip-everything command by office preference. STRIPMTEXT is registered as an alias and does exactly the same thing.
howto: Select the objects first if you like, otherwise it asks for a selection filtered to mtext, multileaders, dimensions and block references. There are no further prompts; it reports StripMtext completed. N objects processed.
produces: Rewrites the contents of mtext, multileader mtext content, dimension text overrides and block attribute values. Mtext columns are collapsed so the text reflows as one block.
notes: Line breaks (\P) are kept — they are content, not formatting — as are escaped literals. Stacked fractions become readable a/b text. Background masks are a property rather than an inline code, so they are left alone.

summary: Add a prefix or suffix to selected text, mtext, multileaders and dimensions
body: Bulk-edits a selection of annotation by putting the same string in front of or behind each item — adding units, an approx. qualifier or a diameter symbol across a set of labels in one go.
howto: Select the entities first if you like. It asks Add text as [Prefix/Suffix], defaulting to Suffix, then Text to add: (spaces allowed). If nothing was pre-selected you're then asked to Select text entities:, filtered to text, mtext and multileaders. An empty string cancels.
produces: Edits the existing entities in place; nothing is created.
notes: For dimensions, a measurement with no override is represented as the <> placeholder so a prefix or suffix keeps the live measured value rather than freezing it. The engineering and drafting plugins both carry this command; the implementations are identical, so having both installed is harmless.

summary: Create one plot-ready layout per selected raster sheet, with the image stretched to the paper
body:
Turns a folder of scanned or exported design sheets into a set of layouts — one per image, named after the file, with the image stretched to fill the sheet and the page already set up to plot.

This is the starting point for a works-as-executed job: import the design sheets, then mark them up in red.
howto: Run it and answer Specify sheet size [A4/A3/A2/A1]: — Enter takes the A1 default. A file dialog opens (at the drawing's Rasters folder if there is one) where you can select many images at once. If some of them already have layouts you're asked once, N of the selected sheet(s) already have layouts [Replace/Skip]:, defaulting to Skip. Progress is reported per sheet and it finishes on the first layout it created.
produces: A layout per image, its default viewport erased and the raster attached on the SHEET layer, stretched to the paper size. Each layout is configured for Print As PDF.pc3 at the chosen media, millimetres, rotated 90°, centred, plot type extents, with the BW_FINAL.ctb plot style table shown, and opens zoomed to extents.
notes: The whole import is one undo group — a single U removes every layout it made. Characters that layout names can't hold are replaced with hyphens, and a file whose name leaves nothing usable is skipped. If the PDF plot device is missing the sheets still import at standard ISO sizes, but you're warned once that the plot setup was skipped.

summary: Place WAE label text horizontally at 0°, ignoring the drawing's angle base
body: Quick annotation on a WAE sheet at a fixed horizontal rotation, so you can letter a rotated or imported sheet without fighting the UCS or the drawing's angle base.
howto: Run it, answer Text insertion point:, then type the text in place and finish as normal. Because the WAE LABEL style has a fixed height you are never asked for one.
produces: Single-line text at 0°, top-left justified, on layer ANNOTATIONS in the WAE LABEL style (Lucida Sans Unicode, fixed 2.5 height — not annotative, because WAE sheets are worked at paper scale). Colour, linetype and lineweight are set ByLayer.
notes: ANGBASE is temporarily zeroed so the text lands at a true 0° whatever the drawing's angle base is, then restored when the text command ends.

summary: Place WAE label text vertically at 270°, ignoring the drawing's angle base
body: The vertical companion to HTXT — for labelling down the side of a sheet or along a vertical feature.
howto: Run it, answer Text insertion point:, then type the text in place. No height prompt — the WAE label style has a fixed height.
produces: Single-line text at 270°, top-left justified, on layer ANNOTATIONS in the WAE LABEL style at its fixed 2.5 height.
notes: Like HTXT, it zeroes ANGBASE for the placement and restores it afterwards.

summary: Rotate selected text 180° about its middle centre so it reads the right way up
body: Fixes annotation that has ended up upside down — usually after a marked-up sheet has been rotated. Rotating about the middle centre means the text stays where it was rather than swinging away from the feature it labels.
howto: Select the text first if you like, otherwise it asks for a selection filtered to text and mtext. No further prompts; it reports Text flipped 180 degrees with Middle Center attachment.
produces: Edits the selected entities in place: attachment or justification is set to middle centre and the rotation is increased by 180°.
notes: The justification change is permanent, so flipping twice returns the text to its original angle but not to its original justification.

summary: Place the standard surveyor certification note on a works-as-executed front sheet
body: Writes the office certification paragraph in full, with the registered surveyor's name and the surface layer filled in — the block of text that goes on the front sheet of every WAE set.
howto: Three prompts: Select Surveyor [Ben/Angela/Peter]:, which expands to the surveyor's full registered name; Select Surface type [First/Second/fInal]:, the AC layer the road centrelines were taken on; then Specify point to place text:.
produces: One MText block 150 units wide at 2.5 height in the WAE LABEL style, on layer ANNOTATIONS. It covers the work-as-executed certification, interallotment drainage within easements, the road centreline layer, Australian Height Datum, and pit and pipe sizes being as per design — followed by a signature rule and a line reading ADD DATE AND COMMENTS HERE.
notes: The surveyor list is fixed in the command. A name that isn't on it has to be typed over afterwards.

summary: Work out the percentage grade between two levels over a chainage and label it
body: Computes a grade from two levels and a distance and places the result as a labelled percentage, so pipe and road grades can be annotated straight off the surveyed levels without a calculator.
howto: It loops so you can do several in a row. For each grade: Select first level or press Enter to input manually: — pick a text entity and the first number in it is read out, or press Enter and answer Enter first level:. The same for the second level. Then Choose chainage method [Direct/Calculate]: — Direct asks Enter chainage directly:, Calculate asks for a first and second length and uses the absolute difference, echoing what it worked out. Finally Specify point to place <grade> grade text:, with the computed value already shown in the prompt. Esc finishes.
produces: MText at 2.5 height, middle-centre, in the WAE LABEL style on layer ANNOTATIONS, reading the grade to one decimal place with a percent sign — for example 1.5%. The calculation is (first level − second level) ÷ chainage × 100.
notes: A chainage of zero is rejected — it says Chainage cannot be zero. and starts the cycle again rather than failing. A selected text with no number in it gives Invalid selection, try again.

summary: Add a prefix or suffix to selected text, mtext and multileaders on a WAE sheet
body: Bulk-edits marked-up annotation by adding the same string to the front or the back of each selected item.
howto: Select the text first if you like, otherwise it asks for a selection filtered to text, mtext and multileaders. Then Choose [Prefix/Suffix]: and Enter text for Prefix/Suffix: (spaces allowed). It reports Modification completed.
produces: Edits the selected entities in place; nothing is created. Multileaders are only edited when their content is mtext.
notes: This is the WAE ribbon's own command. The engineering and drafting ribbons carry TADD, which does the same job and also handles dimension text.

summary: Insert the WAE tick symbol block repeatedly until you press Esc
body: Drops the standard WAE tick — the mark used to sign off items checked against the design — as many times as you need in one run.
howto: Run it and answer Specify insertion point: for each tick. It keeps asking until you press Esc.
produces: Block references of the waetick block on layer ANNOTATIONS, with colour, linetype and lineweight ByLayer. The block definition is imported from Support\waetick.dwg beside the plugin on first use and reused afterwards.
notes: If the block drawing is missing you get [BW WAE] waetick.dwg not found beside the plugin — reinstall the WAE component.

summary: Open the NSW Cadastral Lot Loader panel to fetch lot boundaries and labels from NSW Spatial
body:
Opens the lot loader, which pulls cadastral boundaries, lot labels, road names and road centrelines straight from the NSW Spatial service into model space. Lots can be found by lot and plan number, by picking a point, or by an extent.

The panel is modeless, so it stays open while you work in the drawing. The ? button in its title bar opens offline help.
howto: The command itself has no prompts — it just shows the panel, and everything happens in the form. Set the import options (subject and adjoining lot labels, road names, road centrelines), choose one of the three searches, and click Fetch Lots. Entries and settings are remembered for next time.
produces: Polylines and MText on the office cadastral layers: SUB BDY and SUB DP for the lots you asked for, ADJ BDY and ADJ DP for neighbours and the surrounding buffer, ROAD NAME and ROAD CL for roads. The By Point and By Extent searches put everything on the ADJ layers. Lots already loaded are skipped rather than duplicated. Each boundary carries the parcel details as NSW_PARCEL xdata.
notes: It needs internet access to the NSW Spatial service. The MGA zone is worked out from the fetched data; if it can't be determined the tool assumes Zone 56 and says so in the status bar — worth checking on a Zone 55 job.

summary: Label already-loaded cadastral lots from the parcel data stored on their boundaries
body: Adds lot labels to boundaries that the lot loader brought in earlier — useful when you imported without labels, deleted some, or want them back after tidying up. It reads the plan details from the xdata the loader attached rather than going back to the web service.
howto: Select the lot boundaries first if you like, otherwise it asks to Select lots to label:, filtered to polylines. It reports [NSWLotLoader] Applied labels to N lot(s).
produces: One MText per lot at an interior point of the boundary, middle-centre at 1.0 height, holding the lot number, section number and plan label on separate lines. Boundaries on SUB BDY are labelled onto SUB DP (yellow); everything else goes onto ADJ DP (white). The layers are created if they don't exist.
notes: It only works on polylines carrying NSW_PARCEL xdata — boundaries drawn by hand or brought in another way are silently skipped. It doesn't check whether a lot is already labelled, so running it twice on the same selection doubles the labels up. There is no ribbon button; type the command.

summary: Toggle the Point Cloud Digitizer panel for tracing features off a point cloud
body:
Shows or hides the digitizer panel, which traces features off a point cloud — stepping along at a fixed distance per vertex, or tracing freely — with every vertex snapped to the cloud, numbered and coded as it goes. Each drawing gets its own panel.

The panel's buttons run the companion commands: PCDIG_LINE (Add Line), PCDIG_POINT (Add Point), PCDIG_EXTEND (Extend an existing 3D polyline) and PCDIG_EXPORT (Export to 12da).
howto: The command itself has no prompts — it toggles the panel. Set the segment distance, point numbering, point code and layer (manually or from a Trimble .fxl feature library) in the panel, then start a run. Digitising prompts Pick point (Esc to exit): with an Undo keyword that steps back a vertex; Extend asks you to Select polyline near the end you wish to extend:.
produces: 3D polylines and, optionally, survey points on the feature's layer — Civil points where the Civil module is available, otherwise standard points with the number and code attached. The layer is created from the feature library's colour if it doesn't exist. Export to 12da… writes the digitised strings and points to a 12d Model ASCII file.
notes: While digitising, 2D object snaps are turned off and point-cloud nearest snapping is turned on, and PDMODE/PDSIZE are set for point visibility if they were at their defaults — all restored when the run ends. A locked target layer stops the run before it starts. The export can't run while a digitising run is active.

summary: Open the drawing QA checklist for the current project, creating it from the office master if needed
body:
Opens the project's drawing checklist — the NSW drafting QA form — for the drawing you have open. If the project doesn't have one yet, a copy is made from the master template bundled with the tool.

The checklist lives two folders up from the drawing, in a 4 Checklists folder, matching the office project layout. The window is modeless so you can work in the drawing while it's open, and only one is live at a time.
howto: No prompts — run it and the checklist window opens. Warnings appear as message boxes: the drawing not being saved yet, or the bundled master template being missing.
produces: Nothing in the drawing. It opens (or creates) Drafting - Drawing Checklist NSW SUR-FO-0615 v1.0.xlsx in the project's 4 Checklists folder.
notes: The button for this sits on the WSY Drafting ribbon's QA panel — there is no button for it on the Engineering, WAE or WSY Tools tabs. Closing a saved drawing that has a project checklist prompts you to complete it first; answering yes opens the checklist modally and holds the close until you're done.
